cohort: Low-risk women (without hypertensive disease or diabetes) with nonanomalous singleton pregnancies, who delivered after labor at 37-41 weeks of gestation in the United States
finding: Modifiable maternal risk factors, including lack of prenatal care, smoking during pregnancy, being overweight or obese, gestational age of 41 weeks, chorioamnionitis, and cesarean or operative vaginal delivery, were associated with neonatal seizures among low-risk pregnancies at term.
mod_finding: The risk of neonatal seizures was higher for operative vaginal and cesarean delivery compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery.
